Performance Tutorial

Optimize your Ifá-Lang programs with CPU parallelism, GPU acceleration, and efficient data structures.

Profiling

Measure before optimizing:

ese benchmark(name, func) {
    ayanmo start = Iwori.akoko_ms();
    ayanmo result = func();
    ayanmo elapsed = Iwori.akoko_ms() - start;
    Irosu.fo(name + ": " + elapsed + " ms");
    padapo result;
}

// Usage
benchmark("Process data", {
    -> process_large_dataset(data)
});

CPU Parallelism

Use the CPU infrastructure for parallel operations on buffers.

Parallel Map

// Allocate a CPU buffer
ayanmo buf = Cpu.alloc_buffer(1000000);
Cpu.write_buffer(buf, [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, ...]);

// Parallel map: square every element
ayanmo result = Cpu.par_map(buf, "square");
ayanmo values = Cpu.read_buffer(result);

// Available par_map operations:
// square, cube, double, inc, dec, neg, abs, sqrt

Parallel Reduce

// Allocate buffer with data
ayanmo buf = Cpu.alloc_buffer(1000000);
Cpu.write_buffer(buf, data);

// Parallel reduce operations:
ayanmo total = Cpu.par_reduce(buf, "sum");
ayanmo min = Cpu.par_reduce(buf, "min");
ayanmo max = Cpu.par_reduce(buf, "max");
ayanmo product = Cpu.par_reduce(buf, "product");

Thread Pool Configuration

// Use all cores (default)
Cpu.configure(Cpu.threads());

// Or limit to specific count
Cpu.configure(4);  // Use 4 threads

GPU Acceleration

For heavy numerical work, use GPU compute (requires gpu feature):

// Initialize GPU
ayanmo gpu = GPU.new();

// Matrix multiplication on GPU
ayanmo a = create_matrix(1024, 1024);
ayanmo b = create_matrix(1024, 1024);

ayanmo buf_a = GPU.create_buffer(a);
ayanmo buf_b = GPU.create_buffer(b);

// Compute on GPU (massively parallel)
ayanmo buf_c = GPU.matmul(buf_a, buf_b, 1024, 1024, 1024);

// Read result back
ayanmo c = GPU.read_buffer(buf_c);

Efficient Data Structures

List vs. Map Lookup

// Slow: O(n) lookup
ayanmo users = [{"id": 1, "name": "Alice"}, ...];
ayanmo user = Ogunda.wa(users, { u -> u["id"] == 5 });  // Scans entire list

// Fast: O(1) lookup
ayanmo user_map = {};
fun u ninu users {
    // maps are key-value stores
    user_map[u["id"]] = u;
}
ayanmo user = user_map[5];  // Direct access

Lazy Processing

// Single pass with early exit
ayanmo result = [];
fun item ninu data {
    ayanmo transformed = transform(item);
    ti (is_valid(transformed)) {
        Ogunda.fi(result, transformed);
        ti (Ogunda.iwon(result) >= 10) { da; }
    }
}

Resource Cleanup with Ebo

ese process_file(path) {
    ayanmo content = Odi.ka(path);
    ebo "file_cleanup";  // Auto cleanup marker
    
    padapo process(content);
}  // Resources released when scope ends

Common Bottlenecks

  • String concatenation in loops - Use Ika.dapo / join
  • Repeated list scans - Build a map for O(1) lookup
  • Synchronous I/O - Use parallel batch operations
  • Creating objects in hot loops - Pre-allocate when possible
